clue.text: Treat superficially books penned by Carry On actor

indicators.note: penned by means held inside, as if written into the other word's enclosure

parts.note: Jim Dale starred in many of the British Carry On comedy films
BB is a standard crossword abbreviation for books

explanation.surface: A critic complains that a comedy actor's books only skim the surface of their subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films were a long-running series of British comedy films; Jim Dale was a regular in them.
explanation.definitionFit: To dabble is to engage with something lightly, without depth or commitment.

clue.text: Stupid clanger? It's raised in gym

parts.note: dumb is informal for stupid
a bell is something that clangs

explanation.surface: A foolish blunder is brought up in the gymnasium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clanger' suggests a British blunder, but here it is literally a thing that clangs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand weight lifted repeatedly during exercise, a classic piece of gym equipment.

clue.text: Record name in neckwear in Italian city

indicators.note: in means placed inside the neckwear word

parts.note: a boa is a long feathery scarf worn round the neck
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A traveller notes a name label on a scarf bought in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bologna is a city in northern Italy, capital of Emilia-Romagna.

clue.text: A good man with depression under 50 is desperate

indicators.note: under means the following pieces sit below the first in this down entry

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
ST, for saint, is a crossword stand-in for a good man
a ditch is a depression or trench in the ground

explanation.surface: A decent man feeling low in his late forties is desperate.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final desperate attempt made when all else has failed.

clue.text: National institution operating amid protest ending in rally

indicators.note: amid means set in the middle of the other word, so one piece goes inside the protest word

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration
on means working or operating, as a machine that is switched on

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of the word rally

explanation.surface: A news report of a protest movement against a national institution, ending in a rally.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchy, with its crown and royal family, is often called a national institution in Britain.

clue.text: What's up among public opposing how some drugs are sold?

indicators.note: among means set amid the other pieces, so it goes between them

parts.note: overt means open and public
counter means opposing or contrary

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: eh is an exclamation asking what was said

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is going on with public opposition to how certain medicines are sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's' stands for the querying exclamation, and 'up' flips it because this is a down entry; 'among' puts the result between the two other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicines bought over the counter need no prescription, unlike those dispensed by a pharmacist on order.

clue.text: A large, worthless musical collection

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
bum is informal for worthless or bad, as in a bum deal

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a big, worthless set of songs.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a collection of musical tracks released together.

clue.text: Is youth able to find dining facility?

parts.note: can means is able to
a teen is a young person

explanation.surface: A question about whether a young person can locate somewhere to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a cafeteria in a workplace or school where meals are served.

clue.text: Variable names devised for compliant figure

parts.note: Y is a letter used for a variable in algebra

indicators.note: devised means freshly put together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Changeable titles are invented for a submissive character.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes man is someone who always agrees with their superiors, an obedient sycophant.

clue.text: Outline of a post

parts.note: post here means a job, and the outline is the document setting out its duties

explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' suggests a pole or the mail; it means a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A document setting out a role's duties sketches what a job involves.

clue.text: Philosopher's vocal character proving a heavy burden

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was a philosopher, so the possessive gives Mill's
tone is the character or quality of a voice

explanation.surface: A philosopher's manner of speaking turns out to be a weight on his listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, a millstone round your neck is a heavy burden or encumbrance.

clue.text: Extra payment that's good in France and America

parts.note: bon is the French word for good
US is the abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A financial term described as something good on both sides of the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is money paid on top of normal wages, an extra reward.

clue.text: Speciality shown by husband and father in ME city

parts.note: your bag is informal for your speciality or thing you do best
dad is an everyday word for father

explanation.surface: A family's speciality is displayed in a Middle Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is short for Middle East, not the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Baghdad is the capital of Iraq, a city in the Middle East.

clue.text: Soften a medium for artists

parts.note: to temper is to soften or moderate something

explanation.surface: An instruction to tone down a go-between used by artists.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a paint made with egg yolk, a traditional painting medium.

clue.text: Smallest amount learner gained with bridge player

parts.note: L is the learner sign on a British learner driver's car
in bridge the four players are named North, South, East and West

explanation.surface: A novice who partners a bridge player wins only the smallest sum.
explanation.definitionFit: The least is the minimum, the smallest quantity possible.

clue.text: Wholesale responsibility of a street cleaner

definitions.meaning: wholesale here means ... in scope, indiscriminate and extensive, as in ... changes
a street cleaner's job is brushing the road with a broom

explanation.surface: Wholesale cleaning of the streets falls to the council sweeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping as an adjective means broad and comprehensive; as a noun it is brushing dirt away.

clue.text: Special number on course to take in alien dance movement

indicators.note: on in a down entry means placed above the following piece

parts.note: pi is the special mathematical constant, about 3.14

indicators.note: take in means hold within, so one piece goes inside the course word

parts.note: a route is a course taken
ET, the film's extraterrestrial, is a standard alien

explanation.surface: A featured routine along the way includes an extraterrestrial ballet move.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a spin on one foot in ballet.

clue.text: Poor track followed by name when climbing

parts.note: a path is a track

indicators.note: climbing in a down entry means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: A rough trail on which a hiker calls out while ascending.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic means feeble or miserably inadequate, a sense of poor.

clue.text: Success with time sealed by brave figure up to now

parts.note: a hit is a success, such as a hit record

indicators.note: sealed by means shut up inside the other word, enclosed on both sides

parts.note: a hero is a brave person

explanation.surface: A tale of success that a hero has kept under wraps until now.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitherto is a formal adverb meaning until this point in time.

clue.text: Dim Pole disorientated in collapse

indicators.note: disorientated means confused and turned around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dim-witted Pole loses his bearings and falls down.
explanation.definitionFit: To implode is to collapse inward violently.

clue.text: A leading performer cycling is religious follower

indicators.note: cycling means the last letter is brought round to the front, as on a wheel turning

parts.note: the star is the lead performer in a show

explanation.surface: A cycling celebrity turns out to belong to a religious movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the final R of ASTAR to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta is a follower of Rastafarianism, a religion that arose in Jamaica.

clue.text: Label son found on watch

parts.note: ticker is slang for a watch, from its ticking

explanation.surface: A tag reveals a boy's name on a wristwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticker is an adhesive label.

clue.text: Pass second river wearing cloak

indicators.note: wearing means the cloak goes around the river letter like a garment

parts.note: a cape is a cloak

explanation.surface: A runner overtakes another by the river while dressed in a cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass can mean a predicament, as in a pretty pass; a scrape is an awkward situation.

clue.text: Centre of heat?

parts.note: the heat is slang for the police, so their centre is the police station

explanation.surface: A physics question about where warmth is concentrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat' looks like temperature, but it is slang for the police; their base is the station.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang name for a police station, the hub where the police work.

clue.text: Check under lid for opening in deck

indicators.note: under in a down entry means the check piece sits below the lid piece

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: An inspector checks beneath the cover of a ship's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatch is an opening in a ship's deck leading below.

clue.text: Hours in ground showing support

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, as coffee is ground, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Time spent working the soil helps plants thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil but signals the anagram of HOURS and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to sustain or support with food or encouragement.

clue.text: Take on party in suitable surroundings

indicators.note: suitable surroundings means the word for suitable encloses the other piece

parts.note: apt means suitable or fitting
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Hosting a party in a fitting venue is something to take on.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a policy or a child is to take it on as your own.

clue.text: I study note with equipment that's formulaic

parts.note: a den is a private room for study or work
ti is a note of the sol-fa scale
kit is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: A student describes studying music with gear that turns out to be predictable.
explanation.definitionFit: Identikit is used figuratively to mean standardised and lacking individuality, as if assembled from stock parts.

clue.text: Neat help devised for one with trunk

indicators.note: devised means worked out or put together anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidy aid has been invented for someone with luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant is the animal famous for its long trunk.

clue.text: Relating to a post-imperial system?

parts.note: imperial units of measure were replaced in Britain by the decimal system of metres and kilograms

explanation.surface: A history question about how a nation was governed after its empire ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imperial' suggests empire, but it is the old British system of measures (feet, pounds) that metres replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: The decimal measuring system based on metres succeeded imperial units in Britain.
